frontier: OEIS A385316: what is a(6), the smallest integer representable as a sum of three prime cubes in exactly 6 ways? Census at C=10^9 found max multiplicity 4; a(6) > 10^9.
action:
Milestone: verifier_construction; contract=sha256:8d51fc61fba0b1e156ad8e3f452b419d28072672bca2b1a6f006cf81817c23cc
Wrote verifier_a385316.py as a self-contained, no-network Python replay entrypoint. Implemented two independent rejection branches: (1) domain validation — checks that all three components of a candidate (p,q,r) are prime via deterministic Miller-Rabin; (2) predicate validation — enumerates all unordered triples of prime cubes summing to N and verifies exact multiplicity k. Fixed a bug in the known-good replay where max_N was derived from dict keys instead of values, which prevented reproducing a(2)..a(4). Ran kill-fixture replay: one domain kill fixture (composite triple 9,25,49 → rejected with domain violation) and two predicate kill fixtures (N=24 claimed k=2, actual 1; N=185527 claimed k=3, actual 2 → both rejected with predicate violations). All 4 known-good terms (a(1)=24, a(2)=185527, a(3)=8627527, a(4)=999979163) reproduce exactly.
